label: thm:analyticblock
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
According to \cite[Chp. 2 \S 1.4]{Kat1976}, the eigenspace
    \[ M(p) = \text{span}\left(\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\Gamma}(zI - A(p))^{-1}dz\right)\]
    is an analytic vector bundle, where $\Gamma$ is defined in \Cref{assumptionblock}. As $E_{\rho}$ is open and simply connected, the vector bundle $M(p)$ is holomorphically trivial, hence, thanks to \cite[Thm. 30.1]{For1981}, there exist $m$ 
    global holomorphic sections $[\boldsymbol{x}_1(p), \dots , \boldsymbol{x}_m(p)] \in M(p)$ such that for
   each point $p \in E_{\rho}$ the vectors $[\boldsymbol{x}_1(p), \dots , \boldsymbol{x}_m(p)]$ are linearly independent.

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is the same as for \Cref{thm: convergence} and \cite[Thm 3]{Gui2024} but, for bounding $\|C_x - C_p\|_2$ we use that 
    \[ \sigma_{\min}(Q_R(\boldsymbol{p}_{cheb})) \geq \sqrt{\frac{r-1}{2}}\]
    as stated in \cite{Str1999}, also reported in \cite{Dem2019}. The $Q_R(\boldsymbol{p}_{cheb})$ is the matrix whose entry $(i,j)$ is equal to the $j$-th Chebyshev polynomial evaluated at the $i$-th Chebyshev point.

label: thm: asymptoticrate
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The first two points are already proven in \Cref{thm: convergencecheb} in the non-asymptotic case. An alternative proof can be derived as the logarithmic potential for the arcsine measure is \cite[Def. 3.4]{Saf2010}
    \[ U^{\mu}(z) = \log(2) - \log|z + \sqrt{z^2 - 1}|\]
    for $z \notin [-1,1]$ while it is $\log(2)$ if $z \in [-1,1]$. It follows that
    \[ \exp(-r(U^{\mu}(p_*) - \max_{z \in \Gamma} U^{\mu}(z)) = \exp(-r(U^{\mu}(p_*) - \log(2) + \log(\rho)))\]
    where we have used that $U^{\mu}(z) = \log(2) - \log(\rho)$ for $z \in \Gamma$ as $\partial E_{\rho}$ is a level curve for $U^{\mu}(z)$. This is equal to $\rho^{-r}$ if $p_* \in [-1,1]$, while, if $p_* \notin [-1,1]$, it is equal to
    \[\exp(-r( - \log(|p_*| + \sqrt{p_*^2 - 1}) + \log(\rho)) \]
    If $\mu$ is the uniform measure, we assume that $\rho$ is large enough so that we can use 
    \[ \max_{z \in \Gamma} U^{\mu}(z) \approx -\log(\rho/2).\]
    On the other hand, $U^{\mu}(z)$ is not constant over $[-1,1]$ and it is equal to
     \[ U^{\mu}(z) = -\frac{1}{2}\int_{-1}^1 \log(|z - x|)dx = 1 - \frac{1}{2} \Big[ (z + 1)\log(z + 1) + (1-z)\log(1-z) \Big].\]
    The minimum potential is achieved at $1$
    \[ \min_{z \in [-1,1]} U^{\mu}(z) = U^{\mu}(1) =-\frac{1}{2}\int_{-1}^{1} \log|1-x|dx = 1-\log(2).\]
    From this, we get the formula above and the upper bound
    \[  \exp(-r(U^{\mu}(p_*) - \max_{z \in \Gamma} U^{\mu}(z)) \le \exp(-r(1-\log(2) +\log(\rho/2))) = e^{-r}2^r\rho^{-r}2^r = \left(\frac{e\rho}{4}\right)^{-r}.\]
    If $p_* \notin [-1,1]$, we can explicitly compute $U^{\mu}(p_*)$ (assuming $p_* >1$, $p_* < -1$ is the same)
    \[ U^{\mu}(p_*) = -\frac{1}{2}\int_{-1}^1 \log(p_* - x)dx = 1 - \frac{1}{2} \Big[ (p_* + 1)\log(p_* + 1) - (p_* - 1)\log(p_* - 1) \Big]\]
    from which
     \begin{align*}
    &\exp(-r(U^{\mu}(p_*) - \max_{z \in \Gamma} U^{\mu}(z)) = \\
      &=\exp\left(-r(1 - \frac{1}{2} \Big[ (p_* + 1)\log(p_* + 1) - (p_* - 1)\log(p_* - 1) \Big] +\log(\rho/2))\right)
      \end{align*}
     which concludes the proof.

title: Remark
body_md: Note that our problem has a crucial difference from \cite[\S 5.2]{Jon2025}, that is, the bound in \eqref{eqn:firstbound} and in \eqref{eq: bound}, does \textit{not} depend on $A(p)$ but only on $X$. This suggests that we can select rows from $X$ and, if $X$ is not changed, we can keep the same set of rows for different values of the parameter. This is crucial as it guarantees that the only error in the algorithm comes from a poor performance of the snapshot matrix when $p$ varies, and not by subsampling, as long as the subsampling matrix $S$ was chosen well at the beginning.

name: \textbf{Varying $p$

title: Theorem
body_md:
If we subsample using leverage scores with oversampling from $Z \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times r}$
then 
\[ (1 +\varepsilon)\left\|\frac{1}{\sqrt
s}SZ\boldsymbol{x}\right\| \leq \|Z\boldsymbol{x}\| \leq (1 + \varepsilon)\left\|\frac{1}{\sqrt
s}SZ\boldsymbol{x}\right\| \quad \forall \boldsymbol{x} \in \mathbb{C}^r\]
if $S \in \mathbb{R}^{s \times n}$ 
\[ s \ge 2\varepsilon^{-2}r\log(2r).\]
